newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 14.

text.p: Maoris told to wait for wealth: Maoris must wait for the dividends from fisheries assets -- just as Pakehas would -- rather than spend the assets immediately on social problems, Treaty of Waitangi Fisheries Commission chairman Sir Tipene O'Regan says. Page 1.

Peters runs super gauntlet: Treasurer Winston Peters staunchly defended the compulsory retirement savings scheme before an often suspicious audience during a radio talkback programme on Sunday. Page 2.

Anderton's 10 ways to cheat on the scheme: Issuing a list of 10 ways to avoid the payments, Alliance leader Jim Anderton said avoidance would be popular because for every dollar saved privately, a person would receive a dollar less from the state toward their superannuation. Page 2.

Collection cost seen as impediment: The cost of collecting savings for a compulsory retirement savings scheme could hold back economic growth, Manufacturers Federation chief executive Simon Arnold said on Sunday. Page 2.
Inflation figures shape up as next test: The June quarter inflation figure on Tuesday might again test the Reserve Bank's tolerance for easier monetary conditions, economists say. Page 13.
Ceramco pensions added as liability: Ceramco Corporation has added a new liability of $3.8 million to its books after digging deep into the company accounts. Page 13.

Ministry backs oil price report: THe fact the oil industry was deregulated before a recession does not invalidate concerns about an increasing difference between the price of petrol and that of the imported crude product, the Commerce Ministry says. Page 14.

NZ find stuns world of science: New Zealand scientists have stunned overseas researchers by identifying a key gene which allows males to outgrow females and has far-reaching implications for medicine and agriculture.
Thistle pricks BIL: Hotel chain stuck in the doldrums: Brierley Investments is once again being pricked by its near nemesis Thistle Hotels.
Thumbs down for Hong Kong -- poll: Hong Kong will be a less attractive place to do business now that it is under Chinese rule, a significant proportion of senior business leaders say.
Meat industry targets ACC: The meat industry is looking at taking over a large chunk of Accident Compensation Corporation administration work, as a way of reducing costs.
Airport gets valued: The Minister of Finance, Bill Birch, is expected to receive a report by Merrill Lynch this week on the valuation of the crown's stake in Auckland International Airport.
Camera snaps dairy robber in act: A man brandishing a claw hammer was caught in the act by a surveillance camera as he tried to rob a Beckenham diary on Saturday.
Attack at book launch: Violence and obscene exposure are no way to protest, says Labour MP Mike Moore after an Auckland book launch on Saturday was marred by Maori protesters.
